bio.summary: Jamieson is a cybersecurity consultant seeking a Boulder council seat. His campaign focuses on code reform, fiscal oversight, housing and wildfire preparedness.

statements.text: Downtown has lost roughly 19% of its property value and 10% of its sales tax revenue since 2019, turning our civic and commercial heart from an economic engine to a net drag on the general fund.
statements.speaker: Ryan Jamieson

statements.text: I think the DDA is the right tool for the job from a financial standpoint, but I also think that the city needs to overhaul much of the municipal code that makes doing business in Boulder outrageously expensive and more complex than it needs to be.
statements.speaker: Ryan Jamieson
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Ryan Jamieson

statements.text: When you look through the handy “Budgeting for Resilience and Equity Dashboard” each department provides via PowerBI, it’s not clear that many departments have or understand their priorities.
statements.speaker: Ryan Jamieson

statements.text: In my time in corporate spaces, I found regular meetings with key constituencies was really the simplest way to ensure that everyone was aware of what was underway and what was coming down the pipe.
statements.speaker: Ryan Jamieson
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Ryan Jamieson

statements.text: Ryan Jamieson is running for Boulder City Council on a platform of climate resilience, simpler zoning, fiscal stewardship and housing affordability.
statements.speaker: Boulder Reporting Lab reporter

statements.text: Yes. We need the ability to build more diverse housing types by right in residential areas, plus an easier process to change zoning.
statements.speaker: Ryan Jamieson

statements.text: According to Jamieson, he believes the city does need more housing “of diverse types.” He added that there’s a “big leap” between the typically very expensive single-family home in Boulder and the more affordable smaller condos in town.
statements.speaker: Richard Valenty reporting Ryan Jamieson’s interview

statements.text: I think it’s entirely reasonable for businesses anywhere in Boulder to expect the city to enforce existing laws related to public safety.
statements.speaker: Ryan Jamieson
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Ryan Jamieson

statements.text: Yes. I like the idea, I question some of the plans. Iris, in particular, given traffic speeds, volume, the trees, and that bike lane.
statements.speaker: Ryan Jamieson
